subject_line: Eighty numbered poems in Archilochus on the Moon
email_body:
Dear Simon,

I've been reading about Archilochus on the Moon and its shape as a sequence of eighty short, numbered poems, and I was curious how that structure sits beside your later Shearsman books, The Slip and Two Duets with Occasion. I'd love to ask how you decide when a sequence needs numbering, and how your work as a collagist feeds into building a book.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Archilochus on the Moon as 80 numbered short poems (Fortnightly Review); poet/collagist, directs Leicester Centre for Creative Writing (DMU profile); email seen in search result on DMU staff profile

book_title: The Multimodal Writer: Creative Writing Across Genres and Media
subject_line: From Poker Face to The Multimodal Writer
email_body:
Dear Josie,

Your path interests me: five books with Virago, including the novel Poker Face and The Book of Friendship, and then The Multimodal Writer, your Bloomsbury study of writing across genres and media. I'd like to ask how moving between fiction, creative non-fiction and digital forms changed the way you think about a single piece of writing, and what you now tell students about choosing a form.

subject_line: The title of Purl, and the poems behind it
email_body:
Dear Jo,

I came across Purl, your 2020 collection from Shoestring Press, and noticed the journey from your Melos Press pamphlet A Woman in the Queue to a full book. I'd like to ask how the poems in Purl came together, and whether your flash fiction and poems ever start from the same material before taking different forms. Your 2024 introduction on Alice Oswald's work also made me wonder which poets shaped Purl.

subject_line: An actor's ear in Falling Slowly
email_body:
Dear Robert,

I noticed that you came to the novel as a playwright and actor, with Shooting the Moon in 2008 and then Falling Slowly in 2010, both from Hodder & Stoughton. I'd like to ask how working on stage shaped the way you write dialogue and scenes in fiction, and whether either novel began life as something meant for performance.
